scope: Theorem 11.4 (Matching systems) of the manuscript “Uniform bounds for planar polynomial limit cycles” (preprints/uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-limit-cycles-September-24-2026/uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-limit-cycles-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 143 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8ff8e55372a94e4f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 147-148. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each polynomial degree bound d, there are a finite number T(d) and finitely many fixed open analytic systems Fw(pw, xw) = 0, gw(pw, xw) > 0, w ∈ Wd, 147 with the following properties. 1. Their domains satisfy Definition 11.1. Every finite differential and algebraic system generated from these data, with their original ties and domain restrictions retained, has the absolute zero property. 2. For each field V = (P, Q) of degree at most d, all but at most T(d) of its periodic orbits contained in the fixed square of Section 9 have a representation in one of these systems. The parameter value pw(V ) is the same for every orbit using the same word and preparation choices; endpoint-dependent quantities are unknowns with graph ties. 3. At a representation of a hyperbolic periodic orbit, Fw,xw has full row rank. In each fixed nonzero- minor chart, different represented hyperbolic orbits lie on different connected components of the fiber at pw(V ). The minor charts and their additional margins also satisfy the first assertion.
